correctness.rationale: For the 14-vertex, 21-edge Heawood incidence graph, the unordered two-particle Abrams cubical model has exactly 91 vertices, 252 edges, and 168 squares. Independently reconstructed integral boundaries obey d1*d2=0, rank(d1)=90 and Smith invariants of d2 1^153,2^1,0^14, yielding H0=Z,H1=Z^8+Z/2,H2=Z^14. The specified GL3(F2) action fixes incidence via p->Ap and l->A^{-T}l. Signed cellular traces on all 168 matrices, including orientation reversal on two-cell coordinates, give H2 character (14,-2,-1,2,0) by orders 1,2,3,4,7. The source first-homology trajectory map and mod101 rank check identify H1(Q)=Steinberg8, and subtraction plus the classical PSL2(7) table identifies H2(Q)=W6+Steinberg8, no invariant vectors. The independent integer SNF and all-group signed character check succeeded; the source's rank101 trajectory-map check was inspected rather than independently replayed.

originality.rationale: Earlier graph braid configuration-space works determine discretization, certain ordered and nonequivariant homology results but do not supply this degree-two rational GL3(F2)-character of unordered Heawood configurations in inspected material. The Heawood independence complex has a W6 representation but is topologically a distinct space, while dodecahedral UConf2 studies have another graph and symmetry group. The rational representation is a motivated refinement rather than a new claim for ordinary homology.
